title: US cotton quota faces Brazil's cost edge in Asia
summary:
US Section 301 duties add a cotton tariff-rate quota for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia garments made with US-origin fibre.
US cotton still lands in Asia about five cents per pound above Brazilian bales, limiting the duty benefit for mills and sourcing teams.
Pending verification rules will decide whether the quota shifts fibre buying or mainly reshapes export documentation.

title: India-EU FTA sets CBAM framework for MSME exporters
summary:
India-EU FTA text includes a dedicated CBAM annexure with a work plan for flexibility, compliance and carbon-price engagement.
The framework matters for MSME exporters facing EU verification and embedded-carbon reporting requirements.
The commerce ministry plans district-level and electronic outreach before the pact is signed later this year.

title: Texworld NYC day 1 highlights AI, sourcing and sustainability
summary:
Texworld NYC’s opening day highlighted how AI, connected data and collaboration are reshaping sourcing decisions amid tariff uncertainty. 
Speakers stressed the need to combine cost, supply chain and market intelligence with sustainability and regional manufacturing. 
FW 2027/28 trend forecasts also showcased innovative materials, responsible production and evolving consumer preferences.

title: UK holds Bank Rate at 3.75% as energy prices stay volatile
summary:
The Bank of England kept Bank Rate at 3.75 per cent after a 6-3 MPC vote, with three members backing a rise to 4 per cent.
Volatile Middle East-linked energy prices may lift UK CPI later this year, affecting costs and demand visibility for apparel and textile supply chains.
The MPC sees upside inflation risks but little evidence so far of wage and price second-round effects.

title: US Federal Reserve holds rates at 3.5 to 3.75%
summary:
The Federal Open Market Committee said it kept the federal funds target range at 3.5 to 3.75 per cent and will maintain ample reserves.
The 9-3 vote leaves the US policy-rate backdrop unchanged for textile, apparel and retail supply-chain firms tracking financing conditions.
The committee cited solid activity, strong productivity and capital investment, but said inflation remains elevated.

title: Barmag launches 6020 ceramic oiler for low-titer polyamide yarns
summary:
Barmag’s new 6020 ceramic oiler targets PA6 and PA6.6 low-titer yarns (5–100 denier), improving spinfinish application, yarn quality and process stability. 
The integrated ceramic shaft and optimised yarn guidance reduce spray-off, contamination and filament damage. 
Customer trials showed spray-off-free processing and around 23 per cent higher spinfinish application than conventional solutions.

title: PERFORMANCE DAYS to unveil sustainability exchange platform
summary:

title: Germany's Adidas posts record Q2 revenue, raises FY26 sales outlook
summary:
Adidas reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of €6.7 billion (~$8.90 billion), up 13 per cent year on year, driven by strong direct-to-consumer growth, robust apparel demand and FIFA World Cup momentum. 
Operating profit rose to €574 million, while DTC sales increased 25 per cent.

title: Jack orders 2,000 humanoid robots, testing apparel’s labour model
summary:

Sourcing teams will track payback, throughput, defects, rival machinery moves and industry responses to judge adoption.

summary:

summary:
PDS and Indonesia’s Busana have formed a six-country apparel sourcing partnership spanning Asia, Central America and Italy.
The model lets brands shift orders as tariffs, costs, capacity and delivery needs change, reducing reliance on single-country suppliers.
US buyers are increasing CAFTA-DR sourcing and favouring strategic vendor consolidation.

title: Bangladesh garment bodies seek temporary CNG relief from govt
summary:
Two garment trade bodies in Bangladesh have called for temporarily allowing export units to collect CNG in cylinders from filling stations to keep production running.
The request follows an acute gas shortage after the shutdown of a floating LNG terminal at Moheshkhali and Titas instructing filling stations to stop selling CNG in open cylinders or gas cascade cylinders not mounted on authorised vehicles.

summary:

title: July 28 customs cliff locks in new import costs
summary:
The July 28 customs-entry cutoff has ended the in-transit exemption for qualifying ocean cargo under new US Section 301 forced-labour duties.
Apparel and textile importers missing the deadline now face 10 or 12.5 per cent added duty on affected shipments already at sea.
Sourcing teams must revisit landed costs, supplier mix and purchase orders as USMCA and CAFTA-DR routes gain pricing advantage.

title: America’s closest apparel suppliers lost share despite 36.5-point edge
summary:
Mexico and CAFTA-DR’s US apparel share fell from 13.86 per cent in 2015 to 12.74 per cent in 2025 despite duty and speed.
Regional trade is locked in T-shirts and sweaters, at over 52 per cent of value; women’s woven fashion and outerwear remain marginal.
For buyers, preferences preserve basics programmes but investment gaps in fabrics, finishing and development cap nearshoring gains.

title: The African divide behind AGOA’s 14.1% apparel fall
summary:
US apparel imports from matched AGOA suppliers fell 14.1 per cent to $484.1 million in January-May 2026.
Madagascar and Lesotho drove most losses, while Kenya rose 5.5 per cent, pointing to selective sourcing shifts.
Knitwear carried 71.1 per cent of the net decline, hitting high-volume factory categories.
December expiry leaves 2027 orders and textile investment exposed.
